ai.description: *Cyrtodactylus albofasciatus* (Gekkonidae) reaches 70 mm SVL. It is brown with distinct, white-edged dark transverse bands and a white nuchal collar. Key features include a slender body and tuberculate skin.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Cyrtodactylus albofasciatus* is uniquely distinguished by the presence of a distinct, broad white nuchal collar immediately behind the head, lacking in other Indian congeners.
ai.habitat: *Cyrtodactylus albofasciatus* inhabits the moist deciduous and evergreen forests of the Western Ghats, typically found at low to moderate elevations on rocky outcrops.
ai.behavior: Boulenger’s Indian gecko is strictly nocturnal, emerging after dark to forage for small insects and invertebrates among rocky outcrops and forest floors.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Cyrtodactylus albofasciatus* is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of two hard-shelled eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, generally from June to August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Cyrtodactylus albofasciatus* is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, primarily occurring in the states of Maharashtra, Goa, and Karnataka at low to moderate elevations.
